mechanisms.statement: A token cap turns unfinished reasoning into a non-answer, and the count hides which cut answers would have been right. Scoring 32k text at 16k equals a 16k run. Late finishes are right at a model-specific rate (Think-SFT ~25%, RL ~10%, base ~6%). Under a vote a cap hit abstains, protecting a lone right ballot; finishing it adds mostly wrong ballots. A format that lengthens traces (Think-SFT's native ChatML) loses more at 16k, not at 32k.

holds_against.why: Think-SFT's fresh vote gains +15 over one sample despite 46 % cap hits because the capped samples abstain and leave the right finished ones to win, which is the abstention effect

mechanisms.statement: A plurality-vote count is a sum over problems of P(the right value is the largest group | the problem's right share and its largest wrong-value share). The cued base's MATH-500 problems are bimodal (33 at 0 of 4, far above binomial), so extra votes convert only a middle band of problems near half right, then flatten well below pass@k. A model that abstains at the cap votes near its pass@k already.

mechanisms.statement: An edit is stored in bf16, so the cell measured is not the cell named. Round-to-nearest erases scaled entries below half an ulp: most RL-minus-base entries are one ulp, so a=0.25 acted as about 0.12, and a=0.125 keeps only multi-ulp entries, about a quarter of the nominal push. Stochastic rounding keeps the mean but adds per-GPU noise. Small full-delta doses therefore fall well below the dose curve; rank-8 edits at 1x or more are unaffected.

mechanisms.statement: How far an intervention moves a count depends on how many items of the set are in the middle difficulty band and how many have long solutions. MATH-500 is about 80 % saturated with few cap-prone problems, so a change that moves hard328 by 13 moves cued MATH-500 by about 4, and cap-hit counts scale with the long-problem share. Code sets saturate near 400 of 538 because MBPP+'s strict hidden tests cap every strong 7B model.
